content: Page history is the sole method to track changes made to a specific page. You can access the page history by clicking the link located between the edit and move links at the top of the page. The history will display a list of edits, which can vary in length. By default, fifty edits are shown per history page, but this can be increased to five hundred. Each row in the history typically contains the following elements: (cur): This link allows you to view the differences between the selected edit and the current version of the page. (last): This link shows the differences between the selected edit and the one immediately preceding it. Radio buttons: Two radio buttons are present for each edit, arranged in two columns. By selecting one button from each column and clicking the Compare Selected Versions button, you can compare the chosen edits and view their differences. Timestamp (e.g., 18:00, 15 April): This indicates the exact time the edit was made. A new day is also marked on the history page. Editor (e.g., Mia Kristos): This is the username of the individual who made the edit. m: If an m appears, it signifies that the user marked the edit as minor. Edit summary (e.g., Just a null description.): This is the comment provided by the user regarding their edit. Section title (e.g., ->Section title): If the user edited only a specific section of the page and did not modify the default edit summary, this will indicate the section. The small arrow will take you directly to the edited section. You can browse the history back to the page's creation or, in most cases, back to the last history purge. On the Urban Dead wiki, page histories are occasionally frozen to conserve database space. The Recent Changes link is located in the navigation menu on the left-hand side of any wiki page. Clicking this link displays a list of the most recent changes made to any page in the wiki. The length of the list depends on the options you select at the top of the page. Each row in the list typically contains the following elements: (diff): This link shows the differences between the selected edit and the one immediately preceding it. (hist): This link takes you to the history of the page. Nm.: These symbols provide quick information about the page. N indicates that the page is new, m signifies a minor edit, and . means the edit has not been patrolled. Patrolling indicates that another wiki user (not the author) has verified the edit, which can be done from the diff screen. However, this feature is rarely used in the Urban Dead wiki. Page name (e.g., Help:Editing): This is the name of the page that was edited, along with a link to it. Timestamp (e.g., 12:00): This indicates the time the edit was made. All edits made on a specific date will appear under that date's header. Editor (e.g., Mia Kristos): This is the username of the individual who made the edit. (Talk): This is a link to the user's talk page. Edit summary (e.g., Just a null description.): This is the comment provided by the user regarding their edit. Section title (e.g., ->Section title): If the user edited only a specific section of the page and did not modify the default edit summary, this will indicate the section. The small arrow will take you directly to the edited section. The contributions of any user can be viewed by visiting their user page. On the lower left side of the page, there is a link labeled User Contributions. Clicking this link will take you to a page titled Special:Contributions/ followed by the username. For example, clicking User Contributions while viewing Mia Kristos's user page will take you to Special:Contributions/Mia_Kristos. If you are logged in, you can also view your own contributions by clicking My Contributions in the upper right corner of the page. The User Contributions page is similar to the Recent Changes page, but it only displays edits made by the specific user whose contributions you are viewing. The small arrow will take you directly to the edited section. (top): If this appears, it means the listed edit is still the most recent edit to that page. The Related Changes link is located in the toolbox section on the left side of a wiki page. This feature is similar to Recent Changes, but it only lists changes made to pages that are linked from the current page. For example, clicking Related Changes on this page will display changes to all the Help pages listed in the menu at the bottom of the page. Pages that cannot be edited, such as those in the Special namespace, will not be listed. Clicking this tab will add or remove the page from your watchlist. Alternatively, you can manage your watchlist by clicking Show and Edit complete watchlist on the watchlist page. When a page is on your watchlist, it will appear in bold in most change lists. The watchlist page is similar to Recent Changes, but it only displays changes made to pages you are watching. This option is available in your User Preferences under the E-mail section. When enabled, you will receive an email notification whenever a page on your watchlist is modified. However, you will only receive one email per page change and will not receive further notifications until you visit the page. Keep in mind that wikis are dynamic environments with frequent changes, so consider this when deciding whether to enable email notifications.
